title: Bangladesh has about two decades left of its demographic window
excerpt: A new World Bank report says the working-age share peaks in 2045, while 84% of workers remain in informal jobs.
content:
Bangladesh’s working-age share of the population is projected to peak in 2045, leaving roughly two decades to make the most of it, according to a World Bank report released on Monday, 3 November.

The report, “Demographic Change in South Asia: From Tailwinds to Headwinds for Development”, says Bangladesh is expected to become an aged society by 2051, The Daily Star reported.

Jobs are the constraint

About 84% of Bangladesh’s workforce, roughly 58 million people, work in the informal sector, according to the report.

“Bangladesh’s demographic opportunity depends on what it does now,” said Jean Pesme, World Bank division director for Bangladesh and Bhutan.

The regional picture

South Asia’s working-age population of about 1.17 billion is expected to peak in less than a decade. The region is projected to become aged by 2049. Across South Asia, only 17% of working-age people contribute to a pension scheme, and just 10% of older people receive pension benefits, according to the report.

“South Asian economies are ageing faster and earlier in their development journeys,” said Johannes Zutt, World Bank vice-president for South Asia.

Why it matters

For NGOs and donors, the findings point to skills, women’s employment, social protection and old-age support as areas likely to grow in importance as the population ages.

What to watch

Whether the government reflects the report’s jobs and pension findings in its next budget and social protection plans.

Sources
